Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 104, verses 1–6 (part 1 of 3):

The question is: what is faith? …. We are not giving a jurisprudential explanation or definition of faith here. Our discussion is limited to the nature of faith, its value, and its effects on life.

Faith is in fact the connection that this small, limited, human creature establishes with the Reality that is eternal, everlasting and abiding, which is the origin of this universe and from which this universe came into existence. For this reason, this human being also becomes connected with the universe, in that both have one Creator. Then this human being becomes connected with the laws of nature according to which this world runs, and he becomes connected with the forces that operate in this universe. He comes out of the shell of his petty and limited self and enters into the vastness of the universe. In this way he steps beyond the bounds of his limited power and enters into the limitless forces that exist within this universe. The universe is so large in comparison to man that its boundaries are themselves beyond the reach of human knowledge. Then man steps out of the circle of his limited lifespan and enters the limitless times of existence and the times that come after the Resurrection.

The connection of human beings, which grants them this strength, this vastness and this freedom, also grants them the taste to enjoy this entire universe and its beauty, and to see the creatures that love his soul. Because of this connection, the brief journey of life becomes for man a journey of recreation, or a stroll through an exhibition that Allah has adorned for this human being in every place, every spot and every age. The truth is that this is a very great good fortune, a supreme joy and recreation, and a friendship with this whole universe. It is a wealth compared to which no other wealth has any value. It is also such a loss that if anyone is deprived of it, there is no greater loss or deficit than this.

Furthermore, the basic elements of faith are also the basic constituent elements of humanity:

(1) Through the worship of one God, a person is freed from all obedience, servitude and worship other than that of the One God. Thus the idea arises among people that all servants have one standing and are equal to one another. Therefore, it is not a reasonable attitude that a person should be granted the true blessing of freedom! This is the freedom that springs from the human conscience, and springs from the concept that exists as a real and factual truth, and that concept is that in this universe there is only one real power and one real object of worship. Accordingly, the natural demand of this conception of life and conception of the universe is that man be free, and the logical result of this belief is also that man be free.

(2) A person develops divinity (rabbaniyyah), and he derives all his concepts, all his values and standards, all his preferences, and his entire constitution and law from Allah. His relationships with Allah, with this universe, and with people are arranged in accordance with Allah's commands and laws. His personal desires and personal interests vanish from his life, and in their place Allah's Shariah and justice take over. In the consciousness of the believer, the value of his system of life becomes elevated, and his personality rises above the concepts and values of jahiliyyah (ignorance). Jahili preferences come to an end, and all the relationships that are based on earth, this world and material concepts come to an end, even if this person is an individual, because an individual believer too takes his concepts, values and preferences directly from Allah, since these values are indeed more exalted, more honourable, and more beneficial and worthy of consideration.

(3) As a result of faith, the relationship between Creator and creature is also determined. The station of divinity and servitude, of lordship and slavery, is also determined, and this relationship emerges clear and pure. This relationship, which connects a mortal human being with an immortal Being, becomes defined and clear in a very simple and comprehensible manner, and on this path a person no longer needs any intermediary. Through the clarity of ranks, light is created in the heart and tranquility in the spirit. Love and trust are created in the human self. Anxiety, fear, distress and restlessness come to an end. Through this clarity of ranks, a person neither engages in unjust arrogance, nor, by fabricating falsehoods and relying on invented concepts, claims an exalted status for himself over other human beings.

(4) Because of faith, the People of Faith are granted steadfastness upon the Islamic system of life. Therefore, goodness among believers is not a temporary matter, nor an accidental, isolated event. Rather, the Islamic system is an occurrence that has real causes and certain real objectives, and those who run the Islamic system are people connected with one another for the sake of Allah, who support one another. From such people a sound community is formed, which has one single purpose and one distinct banner. This community is a historical community, and its past generations are connected with its coming generations, and its coming generations are connected with the past, and this connection is a strong one.

(5) As a result, the idea arises among people that the human being is highly honoured. The human being himself rises in his own estimation, and within the conscience of the believer there settles a modesty that prevents him from doing any act that would cause him to fall from the rank to which Allah has raised him. This is that lofty and exalted station which no human being could imagine reaching, namely that he is honoured in the sight of Allah. Every religion or philosophical concept that lowers a person in his own eyes and declares him a contemptible creature who came into being by chance, creates distance between man and the higher realm, and such a religion or philosophy lowers man and leads him toward degradation, even if it does not state this explicitly.

Thus the philosophies of Darwin and Freud and the Marxist system were the worst philosophies and systems, which afflicted humanity with the worst calamity and gave it a false direction in terms of humanity, nature and human existence, and made it believe that every degradation, every filth and every contempt is in fact a natural and necessary part of human life. This is not something to be surprised at, so there is nothing to be ashamed of in it. Accordingly, these philosophies and systems are in reality a heinous crime against humanity and deserve to be detested. (Sayyid, has it reached you that all the idols of Marxism have been toppled from the socialist world?)

(6) The mere idea that man is an honoured creature in the sight of Allah purifies human consciousness. Then the idea that Allah is the Overseer of all, and that He knows what is in the breasts, also purifies human consciousness. A sound-natured person, whose nature has not been distorted by the writings of people like Karl Marx and Freud, feels shame at the thought that another human being like himself should be informed of the secrets of his heart and his evil thoughts. And a true believer, who is certain that Allah is aware of all the secrets and hidden things in his breast, trembles at the thought that such and such thoughts are in his heart. Through this, he purifies his consciousness and his feelings, and he also purifies his heart.

The truth is that as soon as faith comes into being, a moral beauty comes into being within the person. He believes that there is one God who is just, merciful, generous and forgiving, forbearing and loving. He does not like evil; He likes goodness. He knows the treachery of the eyes and is aware of the secrets of the hearts.

(7) Furthermore, the idea that man has been given freedom of will, and that alongside this, Allah is keeping complete watch over him, creates within a person awareness and vigilance, and as a result of the understanding and reflection that arise, a person regards himself as a responsible being, and has the right, for every good, that he adopt a responsible attitude with regard to it, and feel responsibility towards other human beings as well. This responsibility is before Allah. Therefore, when a believer makes any movement, his awareness and consciousness are such that he thinks in his heart in every matter and at every step, and he considers the consequences before taking any step, because according to this concept, man is a creature who has a position in this world. Therefore, within the system of this universe, he is a responsible creature.

(8) One important effect among the effects of faith is that a believer does not pounce upon the interests of this world in the way dogs pounce upon bones. One of the indications and effects of faith is that he adopts that which holds lofty purpose in the sight of Allah, that which is "good" and that which endures.

﴿And for this let those who compete, compete﴾ (26:83). "Those who compete should compete in goodness." Competition among one another for the rewards that are with Allah lifts a person above this world, purifies his heart, and makes him pure and clean. Moreover, through this the sphere of a believer's activities expands. He goes beyond the boundaries of this world and is active in the Hereafter as well. Alongside the earth, he also displays his prowess in the higher realm. And this very thing creates in him the strength to continue doing good without caring about results, or not to be hasty about outcomes. For he seeks goodness because it is goodness, and because Allah's pleasure lies in that way. It is not his responsibility that the results of goodness should emerge within this small, limited lifespan. For the Allah for whose sake this goodness is being done is Living; He does not die. He does not forget, and He is not heedless of anything. Furthermore, this world is not the true abode of recompense, and not all accounts are settled in this world. Therefore, the believer draws help, to keep goodness flowing, from a spring that never dries up, and this is why the movement of goodness continues. It is not a momentary enthusiasm, nor an isolated event. It is this faith-based impulse that creates within a believer such strength that he stands against the greatest tyranny, whether this evil takes the form of a single dictator and rebel, or the pressure of jahili concepts and preferences, or the form of the desires of the self. This individual pressure falls upon a person in such a way that he thinks this world is brief, life is short, and one should indulge in pleasure and luxury in it:

"Live in comfort, Babur, for the world does not come again."

Or he thinks that it is so short that the results of good deeds cannot emerge in it, and he does not see any chance that we might witness the triumph of truth over falsehood. Therefore faith cures this condition, and it is the fundamental cure.

The truth is that faith alone is the foundation of life and the root of life, and from it all the branches of goodness spring forth, and every fruit of it hangs from these roots. If faith is absent, it is as though the root of a tree has been cut, and all its branches will wither and dry up. And if they do not dry up, then they will be satanic fruit, and it will not attain permanence or growth.

The truth is that faith is the centre and axis to which all the strings of a high life are connected. If faith is absent, life is an unconnected movement, and without faith this life has no stability or rest. Desires and inclinations pull a person wherever they go.

Faith is in fact a system, and because of it all the scattered deeds become connected with one another, and because of it these deeds come into harmony with one another. They are oriented in one direction, having one movement, one motivating force and one goal.

This is why the Qur'an declares null and void every deed that is not based on this principle, that does not revolve around this axis, and that does not spring from the wellspring of faith. The Islamic theory of life and the Islamic system of beliefs are completely open and explicit in this matter. In Surah Ibrahim it says:

﴿The likeness of those who disbelieved in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes upon which the wind blows violently on a stormy day; they have no power over anything of what they have earned﴾ (18:14). And in Surah al-Nur it says:

﴿And those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level desert, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾ (39:24). These texts clearly indicate that deeds, as long as they are not based on faith, have no value in Islam. The motive beneath deeds should be that the Creator of the universe has commanded them, and their purpose should be to harmonise with the creation of this universe. This is the logical result of the belief which returns all affairs to Allah. Therefore, any deed that has been cut off from faith loses its meaning and value.

(Ustadh Muhammad Abduh, under the verse ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ (8:99), wrote that "some scholars have recorded a consensus (ijma') that no good deed of a disbeliever will benefit him on the Day of Resurrection, and that his punishment will not be lightened; but this is a fundamental matter.") We hold that this issue is not one of consensus, but of the explicit texts of the Qur'an, and the Qur'an and Sunnah are entirely clear on this matter. (Sayyid Qutb)

Faith is evidence that the believer's nature is sound, that the structure of his personality is intact, and that he moves in harmony with the whole of this universe. The nature of the cosmos that surrounds him is in accord with his own, and so he lives within this universe in harmony with it. A believer whose personality is sound has a correspondence with the universe, and this correspondence and unity is the fruit of faith alone. The universe contains proofs and signs showing that one hand of divine power is the Creator of the cosmos. Therefore, if this correspondence between a person and the universe is broken, it is evidence that his personality has been disturbed and that the capacity by which he draws proofs and signs from the universe has been lost. Because of this corruption, the person will remain in loss. Although some deeds may appear to bear the stamp of goodness, without faith these deeds will not be accepted. In short, the world of the believer is broad, comprehensive, long, elevated, beautiful and successful. In contrast, the world of those who are not believers is small, base, low, weak, disappointed and made up of misfortune, and its outcome and end is loss and failure.

﴿And did righteous deeds﴾ (3:103). Righteous deeds are in reality the natural fruit of faith. When faith settles in a heart, righteous action is its inherent movement, just as the heart is in constant motion. Faith is thus a dynamic and positive movement; as soon as it takes residence in a personality, it appears in the form of righteous action. From the Islamic point of view, faith is exactly like this. Islam has no concept of a faith that is extinguished and produces no movement, a faith that is hidden and does not come out of the believer's self in living form. If there is no such natural movement within it, that faith is counterfeit and dead. Faith is a flower whose fragrance cannot be stopped. Wherever there is a flower, fragrance will continue to spread from it. And if a person has no scent of faith, it is as though he does not exist.

From this it becomes clear that faith is the name of movement, action and construction, and all these matters come to the believer from Allah. Faith contains no contraction, nor is it a negative thing. It does not settle in the hidden layers of the conscience, nor is faith the name of good wishes that have no movement behind them. This is the open temperament of Islam, which makes Islam a supreme constructive force, and this power becomes the central driving force within practical life.

This is the meaning of the principle that faith must be connected to the Islamic system of life. The Islamic system of life is the name of a continuous movement that is taking place throughout this entire universe, and this movement has been created by a governing power. It has a goal. To entrust the leadership of humanity to faith means to bring into existence a leadership that produces a method of movement in harmony with the temperament of the whole universe. In other words, it means establishing a good and pure constructive struggle that is worthy of the system of life sent by Allah.

﴿And who enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾ (3:103). Through the practices of enjoining truth and enjoining patience, the features of the Muslim ummah (community) are clearly defined. The organised Muslim community is established along the same lines as the Muslim ummah. It has a distinct existence and personality. Its members have a distinctive bond among themselves. All people share one direction. This ummah or community is also aware of its own existence and keeps its duties before it. This ummah knows what it must do in regard to faith and righteous action, and it knows that from the perspective of faith and righteous action, it must also lead the whole of humanity. Therefore, to counsel one another to truth means that you have to rise up carrying the Amanat-e-Kubra (the Supreme Trust).

In short, from the word "tawasi" (mutual counsel), from its meaning, its temperament and its reality, the existence of the Muslim ummah emerges, or the concept of a united community arises. That is, an ummah that is distinguished, wise, and responsible for establishing truth, goodness, and justice on this earth. Thus this is the most exalted and beautiful picture of the Muslim ummah. Islam desires an ummah of this kind: a distinguished, strong, wise community that watches over truth and goodness, whose members constantly counsel one another to truth and to patience, who live together in mutual love and cooperation, and among whom a special brotherhood prevails. The Qur'an describes this as counsel.

Enjoining truth is necessary because carrying truth is a difficult task. In this world there are countless factors that lead a person away from the path of truth: base desires, expediency, national and family notions, the oppression of tyrants and dictators, the cruelty of oppressors, and the transgressions of those who exceed limits. By counselling one another, remembrance is in fact renewed. People's resolve grows stronger, and unity and harmony arise among the members of the community through shared aims and purposes. In carrying responsibilities, one in fact bears the burden of another. Through counsel, all individual inclinations are gathered together and multiplied many times over, and all those who are guardians and supporters of truth feel that they are not alone. In the work of protecting truth and reality, there are others alongside them. They advise such a person, encourage him, love him, and stand behind him, and they will never let him be disgraced. This religion is in fact the truth, and only a community can protect this religion, a community that knows one another, supports one another, helps one another, and makes up for one another's weaknesses.

Enjoining patience is also very necessary, because remaining on the path of faith and righteous action and watching over truth and justice is a difficult task. It requires patience, perseverance, and a fierce struggle against the factors within the self, and it also requires a struggle against the factors outside the self, and it requires endurance and hardship in the face of the difficulties that come on this path. Likewise, it requires patience in the face of the arrogance and pride of falsehood, patience over the length of the road, patience over the slow pace of success, and patience when the signs of the path disappear and are erased.

Enjoining patience increases human strength, and it creates a collective feeling among people that all of us have one goal and one direction, and in this way everyone finds a support. Workers in this path become close and united as they work together, and they move forward with great resolve, steadfastness, and insistence on their purpose. Moreover, several other collective qualities also arise from this, and these are necessary for the stability of an Islamic community, because Islam cannot survive without a communal atmosphere. The manifestation of Islam also takes the form of a society. If there is no society at all, then there is no Islam, and that would be a complete loss.

The Qur'an established for us a principle, and according to it, a society is declared successful and safe from worldly and otherworldly loss. If we look at the present conditions of the world through the lens of this principle, the frightening picture of the world that appears before us is that the whole world is now suffering complete loss. The most frightening aspect of this loss is that, even before the hereafter, we have fallen into severe loss from a purely worldly point of view. We see that humanity has completely turned away from the goodness whose blessings Allah had made available to people. Moreover, that sovereign authority which was faithful and Islamic, which was founded on goodness and on the principles of truth and justice, has disappeared from this world. The most ugly aspect of this picture is that Muslims, or, to put it more accurately, those people who have fallen very far from that goodness and virtue compared with the other people living on this earth, have moved very far from the system of life that Allah had chosen for them. They have trampled underfoot the constitution and law that Allah had prescribed for them, the one Allah had declared to be the only path to salvation from loss and failure. Especially those regions from which the banners of this goodness were first raised have themselves brought down the banners that Allah had raised for them. These were the banners of faith. And the most unfortunate thing is that the regions from which the banners of Allah's religion were raised have adopted racial nationalism, although the history of this earth bears witness that no nation has ever reached goodness through racial nationalism. The banner of the racial nationalism (Arab nationalism) that these people have raised is something that existed among them even before Islam, but because of it they accomplished no notable achievement on this earth, nor was any of their deeds recorded in the heavens. When Islam came, through the Arabs it raised a banner that was the banner of Allah alone. No other element shared in it. It was in the name of Allah, and even in the name no one shared. It was attributed to Allah alone, with no other attribution. It bore only the colour of Allah, and no other colour. Under the shade of this banner the Arabs attained greatness. They became the leaders of the world. And their leadership was the leadership of goodness: it was a strong leadership, a wise leadership, and a successful leadership in every respect. This was the first time, even in Arab history, that such a transformation succeeded, and in human history too the Islamic revolution was a remarkable success for humanity.

Maulana Abul Hasan Ali Nadwi, in the chapter "Islamic Power and Muslim Leaders" of his famous book "The Influence of the Rise and Fall of the Muslims on the Human World", says:

"The Muslims came onto the field, took the reins of guidance of the world into their own hands, and removed from the office of guidance those sick nations which had seized it and had never used it properly. The Muslims took all the people of the world along with them and began to lead them forward on a balanced and correct course towards their true destination. They possessed all the qualities that proved them worthy of the lofty office of leading all nations, and under their watch and leadership they guaranteed the welfare and felicity of nations.

These distinctive qualities were as follows:

(1) They had the heavenly Book and the divine Shariah. They did not make their own laws or Shariah, because human lawmaking is the source of ignorance, oppression, and errors, and when human beings make laws for human beings, they are altered and amended every day, whereas heavenly books are protected from these errors. The Muslims were safe from blindly stumbling in their daily affairs, in politics, and in leadership, and from groping about in darkness. They had the light of divine revelation to guide them, and all the paths and turns of life were illuminated for them. Every step they took was in the light, and they could see their destined goal clearly. In Surah al-An'am (6:122) it says:

﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness and cannot emerge from it?﴾

They had a divine law and Shariah according to which they judged between people. They were made the standard-bearers of truth and justice, and even in the most severe provocation, anger, enmity, and hatred, they were commanded not to abandon truth and justice, and not to take revenge in matters of truth and justice:

﴿O you who believe, be steadfast in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Let not the enmity of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ (5:8)

(2) They attained to the position of government and leadership after a firm moral training and refinement of the soul. They did not leap from lowliness to loftiness with all their moral defects and shortcomings, as the ordinary ruling nations and holders of power of the world do. Rather, for a long period divine revelation reformed and trained them, and for years they remained under the complete supervision and teaching of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He purified them, fully trained them, accustomed them to a life of abstinence and piety, and made them habituated to chastity, trustworthiness, selflessness and sacrifice, and the fear of Allah. He completely removed from their hearts greed and desire for government and offices. His saying was: 'By Allah, we will not entrust any office to a person who asks for it or who desires it.' Their hearts became completely purified of the desire for elevation, dignity, honour, and the wish for strife and corruption, and in their ears, day and night, these words of the Qur'an resounded:

﴿That is the Home of the Hereafter. We will assign it to those who do not seek haughtiness upon the earth or corruption, and the good outcome is for the righteous.﴾ (28:83)"

Therefore they did not rush to accept positions and offices of government; on the contrary, they avoided accepting them, and at the thought of their responsibilities they would tremble. Whenever any one of them was offered a post, he would draw back and consider himself unworthy of that burden, much less would any of them put forward his own name for government or campaign on his own behalf. Then, when they took up some responsibility, they did not regard it as spoils of war or a morsel of sweet gain, but considered it a trust (amanah) upon them and a trial from Allah. They believed that they had to appear before Allah and answer for every small and great thing. And they would always recite this verse:
﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners, and when you judge between people, to judge with justice﴾ (4:58). "O Muslims! Allah commands you to return the trusts to those entitled to them, and when you judge between people, judge with justice." Also this verse:
﴿And it is He who has made you successors upon the earth and raised some of you above others in degrees, to test you in what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (6:165). "And it is He who made you successors on the earth and raised some of you above others in rank, that He may test you through what He has given you. Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful."

(3) They were not servants of any people, nor representatives of any race or homeland, whose sole concern was the prosperity of that people and race, nor did they believe in the superiority of a particular nation and in granting it leadership and mastery over all nations, holding that "our nation is meant to lead and other nations are meant only to be subjugated." They did not go out beyond the bounds of the Arab world in order to establish an Arab empire over the world and to live a life of comfort and luxury under its shelter, nor to take pride and arrogance over others under its protection. Nor did they go out so that they might free people from the slavery of the Romans and Persians and bring them into the slavery of the Arabs and themselves. They went out only so that they might free the servants of Allah from the servitude of all who are like themselves and bring them into the servitude of Allah alone, without partner. The envoy of the Muslims, Rib'i ibn Amir, proclaimed this truth in the full court of Rustam, the king of Persia. He said: "Allah has sent us so that we may bring people out of the servitude of men into the servitude of the One Allah, and from the narrowness of this world into its vastness, and from the oppression of religions into the justice of Islam." Thus all the nations and all human beings were of one standing in their sight; if there was any difference, it was only of religion. In short, their full practice was upon the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "All people are the children of Adam, and Adam was created from dust. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor a non-Arab over an Arab, except by piety."
And in Surah al-Hujurat, verse 13:
﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ (49:13). "O people! We created you from a male and a female, and divided you into nations and tribes so that you may recognise one another. Surely the most honoured of you in the sight of Allah is the one most mindful of Him."
On one occasion, the son of 'Amr ibn al-'As, the governor of Egypt, struck an Egyptian with a whip and boasted of his father and forefathers. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) ordered the Egyptian to take retribution from him, and said to 'Amr ibn al-'As: "Since when have you enslaved people, when their mothers bore them free?"

These conquerors and rulers never acted with stinginess or narrow-mindedness in bestowing religion, knowledge and civilization, and in matters of government and offices of government they never considered homeland, colour or race. Rather, they were a cloud of generosity that encompassed the whole world, and its bounty was common to all. It watered the entire world, every part of the earth prayed for it, and creatures benefited from it according to their capacity and ability.
Under the shelter and rule of these people, all the nations of the world, without distinction of colour, homeland, religion, knowledge, civilization or government, were given the full opportunity to take their full share and to participate in the reconstruction alongside the Arabs. Indeed, many of their individuals surpassed the Arabs in many virtues, and among them arose imams, jurists and muhaddithin who were themselves the crown of the Arabs and the pride of the Muslims.

(4) Man is a composite of body, heart and intellect. Man cannot attain true success and felicity, and humanity cannot attain balanced progress, until all these faculties of man are nurtured and developed in a proportionate manner, befitting his station. A sound civilization cannot come into existence in the world until there is established a similarly religious, moral, rational and material environment, in which it is possible for man to reach perfection with complete ease. Experience has proved that this is not possible unless the guidance of life and the steering of civilization are in the hands of those who believe in both spirituality and materiality, who are a complete model of religious and moral life, and who are endowed with sound reason and correct knowledge. (pp. 100–164)

And in another section, under the heading "The Period of the Rightly Guided Caliphate," he writes:
"Thus, in history we know of no period more complete and successful in all these respects than the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphate. In that era, spiritual, moral, religious and scholarly resources, material means, and the perfect human being and sound civilization were mutual helpers in bringing into being. Under that government, which was counted among the greatest governments of the world, and possessed a political and material power that surpassed all contemporary powers, exalted moral models and high standards served. Alongside commerce and industry, morality and virtue were also at their full height. Along with the expansion of conquests and the advance of civilization, the progress of both morality and utility also continued. Thus, despite the extraordinary vastness of the Islamic state, the immense growth of its population, and the means and temptations of luxury, crimes and immoral incidents occurred very rarely. The relationship of the individual with another individual, and of the group with its members, was of an astonishing character. This was a standard age, of which the man of a more developed age cannot even dream, and a more blessed and flourishing time cannot be imagined."(p. 167)

These were some features of that blessed era in which humanity, for a brief span, lived under the Islamic constitution laid down by Surah al-'Asr. During that period, people were ruled by a community of believers, who had raised the banners of faith, for whom righteous deeds were their programme, and for whom the counsel of truth and the exhortation to patience were their emblem.

It was a golden age which cannot in any way be compared with the ruin from which all of humanity today suffers. In the struggle between good and evil, all of humanity is afflicted with loss and destruction. All of humanity has closed its eyes to that great good which once the Arabs were the leaders and guides of all humanity; and in the later periods, when they threw down these banners, they became servants of the caravan of humanity, while this caravan too is moving toward the destination of ruin. By the time it has gone, the condition has become that all of humanity has picked up satanic banners, and none of these is a human banner. All of humanity has taken up the banners of falsehood; nowhere is a banner of truth visible. All of humanity has taken up the banners of blindness and misguidance; among them nowhere is a single banner of guidance and light visible. All banners are banners of loss; not even one banner of success is visible. The banner of Allah, through which the Arabs once overspread the world, is still present today. This banner still awaits a hand to raise it. There is need for some community or nation which will walk under this banner on the path of goodness, guidance, reform and salvation.

This is the account of profit and loss in this world. This worldly greatness is in itself a very great success, but if we compare it with the success of the Hereafter, it is very insignificant. The real profit and loss is that of the Hereafter. True profit and loss lie there, because it is a long life, a life that remains forever, and an everlasting abode. The real gain and the real loss are there: Paradise, the gain of Allah's pleasure, or Hell, the loss of Allah's displeasure. In the Hereafter, where a person may have reached his highest level of progress and perfection, or may have so squandered his humanity that he is lost in it, he will fall to the value of a stone, and in comfort and rest he will be lower than a stone.
﴿On the day when every person will see what he has sent forward, and the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾ (78:40). "On the day every person will see what he has earned and sent forward, and the disbeliever will say, 'Would that I were dust.'"

The truth is that this surah points out a decisive and plain path of truth; it shows that all paths are paths of loss, except
﴿Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and enjoined one another to truth and enjoined one another to patience﴾ (103:3). "Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and advise one another to truth, and advise one another to patience." And this is one path; there is no multiplicity in it. It is the path of faith and righteous deeds, the path of establishing an Islamic community, the path of a community which counsels the truth and enjoins goodness, whose ink is truth and whose wages are patience.

The truth is that the path is one. That is why, whenever two companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met each other, they would not part until they had recited Surah al-'Asr. After that, they would say salaam to each other and depart. In effect, they made a mutual covenant that they would follow this revolutionary constitution; they would bind themselves together that they would remain upon the path of righteous faith, continue to counsel the truth and enjoin patience, and pledge that they would remain the guardians of this constitution and members of the community that follows it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 104, verses 1–6 (part 1 of 3):

The question is: what is faith? …. We are not giving a jurisprudential explanation or definition of faith here. Our discussion is limited to the nature of faith, its value, and its effects on life.

Faith is in fact the connection that this small, limited, human creature establishes with the Reality that is eternal, everlasting and abiding, which is the origin of this universe and from which this universe came into existence. For this reason, this human being also becomes connected with the universe, in that both have one Creator. Then this human being becomes connected with the laws of nature according to which this world runs, and he becomes connected with the forces that operate in this universe. He comes out of the shell of his petty and limited self and enters into the vastness of the universe. In this way he steps beyond the bounds of his limited power and enters into the limitless forces that exist within this universe. The universe is so large in comparison to man that its boundaries are themselves beyond the reach of human knowledge. Then man steps out of the circle of his limited lifespan and enters the limitless times of existence and the times that come after the Resurrection.

The connection of human beings, which grants them this strength, this vastness and this freedom, also grants them the taste to enjoy this entire universe and its beauty, and to see the creatures that love his soul. Because of this connection, the brief journey of life becomes for man a journey of recreation, or a stroll through an exhibition that Allah has adorned for this human being in every place, every spot and every age. The truth is that this is a very great good fortune, a supreme joy and recreation, and a friendship with this whole universe. It is a wealth compared to which no other wealth has any value. It is also such a loss that if anyone is deprived of it, there is no greater loss or deficit than this.

Furthermore, the basic elements of faith are also the basic constituent elements of humanity:

(1) Through the worship of one God, a person is freed from all obedience, servitude and worship other than that of the One God. Thus the idea arises among people that all servants have one standing and are equal to one another. Therefore, it is not a reasonable attitude that a person should be granted the true blessing of freedom! This is the freedom that springs from the human conscience, and springs from the concept that exists as a real and factual truth, and that concept is that in this universe there is only one real power and one real object of worship. Accordingly, the natural demand of this conception of life and conception of the universe is that man be free, and the logical result of this belief is also that man be free.

(2) A person develops divinity (rabbaniyyah), and he derives all his concepts, all his values and standards, all his preferences, and his entire constitution and law from Allah. His relationships with Allah, with this universe, and with people are arranged in accordance with Allah's commands and laws. His personal desires and personal interests vanish from his life, and in their place Allah's Shariah and justice take over. In the consciousness of the believer, the value of his system of life becomes elevated, and his personality rises above the concepts and values of jahiliyyah (ignorance). Jahili preferences come to an end, and all the relationships that are based on earth, this world and material concepts come to an end, even if this person is an individual, because an individual believer too takes his concepts, values and preferences directly from Allah, since these values are indeed more exalted, more honourable, and more beneficial and worthy of consideration.

(3) As a result of faith, the relationship between Creator and creature is also determined. The station of divinity and servitude, of lordship and slavery, is also determined, and this relationship emerges clear and pure. This relationship, which connects a mortal human being with an immortal Being, becomes defined and clear in a very simple and comprehensible manner, and on this path a person no longer needs any intermediary. Through the clarity of ranks, light is created in the heart and tranquility in the spirit. Love and trust are created in the human self. Anxiety, fear, distress and restlessness come to an end. Through this clarity of ranks, a person neither engages in unjust arrogance, nor, by fabricating falsehoods and relying on invented concepts, claims an exalted status for himself over other human beings.

(4) Because of faith, the People of Faith are granted steadfastness upon the Islamic system of life. Therefore, goodness among believers is not a temporary matter, nor an accidental, isolated event. Rather, the Islamic system is an occurrence that has real causes and certain real objectives, and those who run the Islamic system are people connected with one another for the sake of Allah, who support one another. From such people a sound community is formed, which has one single purpose and one distinct banner. This community is a historical community, and its past generations are connected with its coming generations, and its coming generations are connected with the past, and this connection is a strong one.

(5) As a result, the idea arises among people that the human being is highly honoured. The human being himself rises in his own estimation, and within the conscience of the believer there settles a modesty that prevents him from doing any act that would cause him to fall from the rank to which Allah has raised him. This is that lofty and exalted station which no human being could imagine reaching, namely that he is honoured in the sight of Allah. Every religion or philosophical concept that lowers a person in his own eyes and declares him a contemptible creature who came into being by chance, creates distance between man and the higher realm, and such a religion or philosophy lowers man and leads him toward degradation, even if it does not state this explicitly.

Thus the philosophies of Darwin and Freud and the Marxist system were the worst philosophies and systems, which afflicted humanity with the worst calamity and gave it a false direction in terms of humanity, nature and human existence, and made it believe that every degradation, every filth and every contempt is in fact a natural and necessary part of human life. This is not something to be surprised at, so there is nothing to be ashamed of in it. Accordingly, these philosophies and systems are in reality a heinous crime against humanity and deserve to be detested. (Sayyid, has it reached you that all the idols of Marxism have been toppled from the socialist world?)

(6) The mere idea that man is an honoured creature in the sight of Allah purifies human consciousness. Then the idea that Allah is the Overseer of all, and that He knows what is in the breasts, also purifies human consciousness. A sound-natured person, whose nature has not been distorted by the writings of people like Karl Marx and Freud, feels shame at the thought that another human being like himself should be informed of the secrets of his heart and his evil thoughts. And a true believer, who is certain that Allah is aware of all the secrets and hidden things in his breast, trembles at the thought that such and such thoughts are in his heart. Through this, he purifies his consciousness and his feelings, and he also purifies his heart.

The truth is that as soon as faith comes into being, a moral beauty comes into being within the person. He believes that there is one God who is just, merciful, generous and forgiving, forbearing and loving. He does not like evil; He likes goodness. He knows the treachery of the eyes and is aware of the secrets of the hearts.

(7) Furthermore, the idea that man has been given freedom of will, and that alongside this, Allah is keeping complete watch over him, creates within a person awareness and vigilance, and as a result of the understanding and reflection that arise, a person regards himself as a responsible being, and has the right, for every good, that he adopt a responsible attitude with regard to it, and feel responsibility towards other human beings as well. This responsibility is before Allah. Therefore, when a believer makes any movement, his awareness and consciousness are such that he thinks in his heart in every matter and at every step, and he considers the consequences before taking any step, because according to this concept, man is a creature who has a position in this world. Therefore, within the system of this universe, he is a responsible creature.

(8) One important effect among the effects of faith is that a believer does not pounce upon the interests of this world in the way dogs pounce upon bones. One of the indications and effects of faith is that he adopts that which holds lofty purpose in the sight of Allah, that which is "good" and that which endures.

﴿And for this let those who compete, compete﴾ (26:83). "Those who compete should compete in goodness." Competition among one another for the rewards that are with Allah lifts a person above this world, purifies his heart, and makes him pure and clean. Moreover, through this the sphere of a believer's activities expands. He goes beyond the boundaries of this world and is active in the Hereafter as well. Alongside the earth, he also displays his prowess in the higher realm. And this very thing creates in him the strength to continue doing good without caring about results, or not to be hasty about outcomes. For he seeks goodness because it is goodness, and because Allah's pleasure lies in that way. It is not his responsibility that the results of goodness should emerge within this small, limited lifespan. For the Allah for whose sake this goodness is being done is Living; He does not die. He does not forget, and He is not heedless of anything. Furthermore, this world is not the true abode of recompense, and not all accounts are settled in this world. Therefore, the believer draws help, to keep goodness flowing, from a spring that never dries up, and this is why the movement of goodness continues. It is not a momentary enthusiasm, nor an isolated event. It is this faith-based impulse that creates within a believer such strength that he stands against the greatest tyranny, whether this evil takes the form of a single dictator and rebel, or the pressure of jahili concepts and preferences, or the form of the desires of the self. This individual pressure falls upon a person in such a way that he thinks this world is brief, life is short, and one should indulge in pleasure and luxury in it:

"Live in comfort, Babur, for the world does not come again."

Or he thinks that it is so short that the results of good deeds cannot emerge in it, and he does not see any chance that we might witness the triumph of truth over falsehood. Therefore faith cures this condition, and it is the fundamental cure.

The truth is that faith alone is the foundation of life and the root of life, and from it all the branches of goodness spring forth, and every fruit of it hangs from these roots. If faith is absent, it is as though the root of a tree has been cut, and all its branches will wither and dry up. And if they do not dry up, then they will be satanic fruit, and it will not attain permanence or growth.

The truth is that faith is the centre and axis to which all the strings of a high life are connected. If faith is absent, life is an unconnected movement, and without faith this life has no stability or rest. Desires and inclinations pull a person wherever they go.

Faith is in fact a system, and because of it all the scattered deeds become connected with one another, and because of it these deeds come into harmony with one another. They are oriented in one direction, having one movement, one motivating force and one goal.

This is why the Qur'an declares null and void every deed that is not based on this principle, that does not revolve around this axis, and that does not spring from the wellspring of faith. The Islamic theory of life and the Islamic system of beliefs are completely open and explicit in this matter. In Surah Ibrahim it says:

﴿The likeness of those who disbelieved in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes upon which the wind blows violently on a stormy day; they have no power over anything of what they have earned﴾ (18:14). And in Surah al-Nur it says:

﴿And those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level desert, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾ (39:24). These texts clearly indicate that deeds, as long as they are not based on faith, have no value in Islam. The motive beneath deeds should be that the Creator of the universe has commanded them, and their purpose should be to harmonise with the creation of this universe. This is the logical result of the belief which returns all affairs to Allah. Therefore, any deed that has been cut off from faith loses its meaning and value.

(Ustadh Muhammad Abduh, under the verse ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ (8:99), wrote that "some scholars have recorded a consensus (ijma') that no good deed of a disbeliever will benefit him on the Day of Resurrection, and that his punishment will not be lightened; but this is a fundamental matter.") We hold that this issue is not one of consensus, but of the explicit texts of the Qur'an, and the Qur'an and Sunnah are entirely clear on this matter. (Sayyid Qutb)

Faith is evidence that the believer's nature is sound, that the structure of his personality is intact, and that he moves in harmony with the whole of this universe. The nature of the cosmos that surrounds him is in accord with his own, and so he lives within this universe in harmony with it. A believer whose personality is sound has a correspondence with the universe, and this correspondence and unity is the fruit of faith alone. The universe contains proofs and signs showing that one hand of divine power is the Creator of the cosmos. Therefore, if this correspondence between a person and the universe is broken, it is evidence that his personality has been disturbed and that the capacity by which he draws proofs and signs from the universe has been lost. Because of this corruption, the person will remain in loss. Although some deeds may appear to bear the stamp of goodness, without faith these deeds will not be accepted. In short, the world of the believer is broad, comprehensive, long, elevated, beautiful and successful. In contrast, the world of those who are not believers is small, base, low, weak, disappointed and made up of misfortune, and its outcome and end is loss and failure.

﴿And did righteous deeds﴾ (3:103). Righteous deeds are in reality the natural fruit of faith. When faith settles in a heart, righteous action is its inherent movement, just as the heart is in constant motion. Faith is thus a dynamic and positive movement; as soon as it takes residence in a personality, it appears in the form of righteous action. From the Islamic point of view, faith is exactly like this. Islam has no concept of a faith that is extinguished and produces no movement, a faith that is hidden and does not come out of the believer's self in living form. If there is no such natural movement within it, that faith is counterfeit and dead. Faith is a flower whose fragrance cannot be stopped. Wherever there is a flower, fragrance will continue to spread from it. And if a person has no scent of faith, it is as though he does not exist.

From this it becomes clear that faith is the name of movement, action and construction, and all these matters come to the believer from Allah. Faith contains no contraction, nor is it a negative thing. It does not settle in the hidden layers of the conscience, nor is faith the name of good wishes that have no movement behind them. This is the open temperament of Islam, which makes Islam a supreme constructive force, and this power becomes the central driving force within practical life.

This is the meaning of the principle that faith must be connected to the Islamic system of life. The Islamic system of life is the name of a continuous movement that is taking place throughout this entire universe, and this movement has been created by a governing power. It has a goal. To entrust the leadership of humanity to faith means to bring into existence a leadership that produces a method of movement in harmony with the temperament of the whole universe. In other words, it means establishing a good and pure constructive struggle that is worthy of the system of life sent by Allah.

﴿And who enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾ (3:103). Through the practices of enjoining truth and enjoining patience, the features of the Muslim ummah (community) are clearly defined. The organised Muslim community is established along the same lines as the Muslim ummah. It has a distinct existence and personality. Its members have a distinctive bond among themselves. All people share one direction. This ummah or community is also aware of its own existence and keeps its duties before it. This ummah knows what it must do in regard to faith and righteous action, and it knows that from the perspective of faith and righteous action, it must also lead the whole of humanity. Therefore, to counsel one another to truth means that you have to rise up carrying the Amanat-e-Kubra (the Supreme Trust).

In short, from the word "tawasi" (mutual counsel), from its meaning, its temperament and its reality, the existence of the Muslim ummah emerges, or the concept of a united community arises. That is, an ummah that is distinguished, wise, and responsible for establishing truth, goodness, and justice on this earth. Thus this is the most exalted and beautiful picture of the Muslim ummah. Islam desires an ummah of this kind: a distinguished, strong, wise community that watches over truth and goodness, whose members constantly counsel one another to truth and to patience, who live together in mutual love and cooperation, and among whom a special brotherhood prevails. The Qur'an describes this as counsel.

Enjoining truth is necessary because carrying truth is a difficult task. In this world there are countless factors that lead a person away from the path of truth: base desires, expediency, national and family notions, the oppression of tyrants and dictators, the cruelty of oppressors, and the transgressions of those who exceed limits. By counselling one another, remembrance is in fact renewed. People's resolve grows stronger, and unity and harmony arise among the members of the community through shared aims and purposes. In carrying responsibilities, one in fact bears the burden of another. Through counsel, all individual inclinations are gathered together and multiplied many times over, and all those who are guardians and supporters of truth feel that they are not alone. In the work of protecting truth and reality, there are others alongside them. They advise such a person, encourage him, love him, and stand behind him, and they will never let him be disgraced. This religion is in fact the truth, and only a community can protect this religion, a community that knows one another, supports one another, helps one another, and makes up for one another's weaknesses.

Enjoining patience is also very necessary, because remaining on the path of faith and righteous action and watching over truth and justice is a difficult task. It requires patience, perseverance, and a fierce struggle against the factors within the self, and it also requires a struggle against the factors outside the self, and it requires endurance and hardship in the face of the difficulties that come on this path. Likewise, it requires patience in the face of the arrogance and pride of falsehood, patience over the length of the road, patience over the slow pace of success, and patience when the signs of the path disappear and are erased.

Enjoining patience increases human strength, and it creates a collective feeling among people that all of us have one goal and one direction, and in this way everyone finds a support. Workers in this path become close and united as they work together, and they move forward with great resolve, steadfastness, and insistence on their purpose. Moreover, several other collective qualities also arise from this, and these are necessary for the stability of an Islamic community, because Islam cannot survive without a communal atmosphere. The manifestation of Islam also takes the form of a society. If there is no society at all, then there is no Islam, and that would be a complete loss.

The Qur'an established for us a principle, and according to it, a society is declared successful and safe from worldly and otherworldly loss. If we look at the present conditions of the world through the lens of this principle, the frightening picture of the world that appears before us is that the whole world is now suffering complete loss. The most frightening aspect of this loss is that, even before the hereafter, we have fallen into severe loss from a purely worldly point of view. We see that humanity has completely turned away from the goodness whose blessings Allah had made available to people. Moreover, that sovereign authority which was faithful and Islamic, which was founded on goodness and on the principles of truth and justice, has disappeared from this world. The most ugly aspect of this picture is that Muslims, or, to put it more accurately, those people who have fallen very far from that goodness and virtue compared with the other people living on this earth, have moved very far from the system of life that Allah had chosen for them. They have trampled underfoot the constitution and law that Allah had prescribed for them, the one Allah had declared to be the only path to salvation from loss and failure. Especially those regions from which the banners of this goodness were first raised have themselves brought down the banners that Allah had raised for them. These were the banners of faith. And the most unfortunate thing is that the regions from which the banners of Allah's religion were raised have adopted racial nationalism, although the history of this earth bears witness that no nation has ever reached goodness through racial nationalism. The banner of the racial nationalism (Arab nationalism) that these people have raised is something that existed among them even before Islam, but because of it they accomplished no notable achievement on this earth, nor was any of their deeds recorded in the heavens. When Islam came, through the Arabs it raised a banner that was the banner of Allah alone. No other element shared in it. It was in the name of Allah, and even in the name no one shared. It was attributed to Allah alone, with no other attribution. It bore only the colour of Allah, and no other colour. Under the shade of this banner the Arabs attained greatness. They became the leaders of the world. And their leadership was the leadership of goodness: it was a strong leadership, a wise leadership, and a successful leadership in every respect. This was the first time, even in Arab history, that such a transformation succeeded, and in human history too the Islamic revolution was a remarkable success for humanity.

Maulana Abul Hasan Ali Nadwi, in the chapter "Islamic Power and Muslim Leaders" of his famous book "The Influence of the Rise and Fall of the Muslims on the Human World", says:

"The Muslims came onto the field, took the reins of guidance of the world into their own hands, and removed from the office of guidance those sick nations which had seized it and had never used it properly. The Muslims took all the people of the world along with them and began to lead them forward on a balanced and correct course towards their true destination. They possessed all the qualities that proved them worthy of the lofty office of leading all nations, and under their watch and leadership they guaranteed the welfare and felicity of nations.

These distinctive qualities were as follows:

(1) They had the heavenly Book and the divine Shariah. They did not make their own laws or Shariah, because human lawmaking is the source of ignorance, oppression, and errors, and when human beings make laws for human beings, they are altered and amended every day, whereas heavenly books are protected from these errors. The Muslims were safe from blindly stumbling in their daily affairs, in politics, and in leadership, and from groping about in darkness. They had the light of divine revelation to guide them, and all the paths and turns of life were illuminated for them. Every step they took was in the light, and they could see their destined goal clearly. In Surah al-An'am (6:122) it says:

﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness and cannot emerge from it?﴾

They had a divine law and Shariah according to which they judged between people. They were made the standard-bearers of truth and justice, and even in the most severe provocation, anger, enmity, and hatred, they were commanded not to abandon truth and justice, and not to take revenge in matters of truth and justice:

﴿O you who believe, be steadfast in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Let not the enmity of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ (5:8)

(2) They attained to the position of government and leadership after a firm moral training and refinement of the soul. They did not leap from lowliness to loftiness with all their moral defects and shortcomings, as the ordinary ruling nations and holders of power of the world do. Rather, for a long period divine revelation reformed and trained them, and for years they remained under the complete supervision and teaching of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He purified them, fully trained them, accustomed them to a life of abstinence and piety, and made them habituated to chastity, trustworthiness, selflessness and sacrifice, and the fear of Allah. He completely removed from their hearts greed and desire for government and offices. His saying was: 'By Allah, we will not entrust any office to a person who asks for it or who desires it.' Their hearts became completely purified of the desire for elevation, dignity, honour, and the wish for strife and corruption, and in their ears, day and night, these words of the Qur'an resounded:

﴿That is the Home of the Hereafter. We will assign it to those who do not seek haughtiness upon the earth or corruption, and the good outcome is for the righteous.﴾ (28:83)"

Therefore they did not rush to accept positions and offices of government; on the contrary, they avoided accepting them, and at the thought of their responsibilities they would tremble. Whenever any one of them was offered a post, he would draw back and consider himself unworthy of that burden, much less would any of them put forward his own name for government or campaign on his own behalf. Then, when they took up some responsibility, they did not regard it as spoils of war or a morsel of sweet gain, but considered it a trust (amanah) upon them and a trial from Allah. They believed that they had to appear before Allah and answer for every small and great thing. And they would always recite this verse:
﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners, and when you judge between people, to judge with justice﴾ (4:58). "O Muslims! Allah commands you to return the trusts to those entitled to them, and when you judge between people, judge with justice." Also this verse:
﴿And it is He who has made you successors upon the earth and raised some of you above others in degrees, to test you in what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (6:165). "And it is He who made you successors on the earth and raised some of you above others in rank, that He may test you through what He has given you. Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful."

(3) They were not servants of any people, nor representatives of any race or homeland, whose sole concern was the prosperity of that people and race, nor did they believe in the superiority of a particular nation and in granting it leadership and mastery over all nations, holding that "our nation is meant to lead and other nations are meant only to be subjugated." They did not go out beyond the bounds of the Arab world in order to establish an Arab empire over the world and to live a life of comfort and luxury under its shelter, nor to take pride and arrogance over others under its protection. Nor did they go out so that they might free people from the slavery of the Romans and Persians and bring them into the slavery of the Arabs and themselves. They went out only so that they might free the servants of Allah from the servitude of all who are like themselves and bring them into the servitude of Allah alone, without partner. The envoy of the Muslims, Rib'i ibn Amir, proclaimed this truth in the full court of Rustam, the king of Persia. He said: "Allah has sent us so that we may bring people out of the servitude of men into the servitude of the One Allah, and from the narrowness of this world into its vastness, and from the oppression of religions into the justice of Islam." Thus all the nations and all human beings were of one standing in their sight; if there was any difference, it was only of religion. In short, their full practice was upon the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "All people are the children of Adam, and Adam was created from dust. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor a non-Arab over an Arab, except by piety."
And in Surah al-Hujurat, verse 13:
﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ (49:13). "O people! We created you from a male and a female, and divided you into nations and tribes so that you may recognise one another. Surely the most honoured of you in the sight of Allah is the one most mindful of Him."
On one occasion, the son of 'Amr ibn al-'As, the governor of Egypt, struck an Egyptian with a whip and boasted of his father and forefathers. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) ordered the Egyptian to take retribution from him, and said to 'Amr ibn al-'As: "Since when have you enslaved people, when their mothers bore them free?"

These conquerors and rulers never acted with stinginess or narrow-mindedness in bestowing religion, knowledge and civilization, and in matters of government and offices of government they never considered homeland, colour or race. Rather, they were a cloud of generosity that encompassed the whole world, and its bounty was common to all. It watered the entire world, every part of the earth prayed for it, and creatures benefited from it according to their capacity and ability.
Under the shelter and rule of these people, all the nations of the world, without distinction of colour, homeland, religion, knowledge, civilization or government, were given the full opportunity to take their full share and to participate in the reconstruction alongside the Arabs. Indeed, many of their individuals surpassed the Arabs in many virtues, and among them arose imams, jurists and muhaddithin who were themselves the crown of the Arabs and the pride of the Muslims.

(4) Man is a composite of body, heart and intellect. Man cannot attain true success and felicity, and humanity cannot attain balanced progress, until all these faculties of man are nurtured and developed in a proportionate manner, befitting his station. A sound civilization cannot come into existence in the world until there is established a similarly religious, moral, rational and material environment, in which it is possible for man to reach perfection with complete ease. Experience has proved that this is not possible unless the guidance of life and the steering of civilization are in the hands of those who believe in both spirituality and materiality, who are a complete model of religious and moral life, and who are endowed with sound reason and correct knowledge. (pp. 100–164)

And in another section, under the heading "The Period of the Rightly Guided Caliphate," he writes:
"Thus, in history we know of no period more complete and successful in all these respects than the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphate. In that era, spiritual, moral, religious and scholarly resources, material means, and the perfect human being and sound civilization were mutual helpers in bringing into being. Under that government, which was counted among the greatest governments of the world, and possessed a political and material power that surpassed all contemporary powers, exalted moral models and high standards served. Alongside commerce and industry, morality and virtue were also at their full height. Along with the expansion of conquests and the advance of civilization, the progress of both morality and utility also continued. Thus, despite the extraordinary vastness of the Islamic state, the immense growth of its population, and the means and temptations of luxury, crimes and immoral incidents occurred very rarely. The relationship of the individual with another individual, and of the group with its members, was of an astonishing character. This was a standard age, of which the man of a more developed age cannot even dream, and a more blessed and flourishing time cannot be imagined."(p. 167)

These were some features of that blessed era in which humanity, for a brief span, lived under the Islamic constitution laid down by Surah al-'Asr. During that period, people were ruled by a community of believers, who had raised the banners of faith, for whom righteous deeds were their programme, and for whom the counsel of truth and the exhortation to patience were their emblem.

It was a golden age which cannot in any way be compared with the ruin from which all of humanity today suffers. In the struggle between good and evil, all of humanity is afflicted with loss and destruction. All of humanity has closed its eyes to that great good which once the Arabs were the leaders and guides of all humanity; and in the later periods, when they threw down these banners, they became servants of the caravan of humanity, while this caravan too is moving toward the destination of ruin. By the time it has gone, the condition has become that all of humanity has picked up satanic banners, and none of these is a human banner. All of humanity has taken up the banners of falsehood; nowhere is a banner of truth visible. All of humanity has taken up the banners of blindness and misguidance; among them nowhere is a single banner of guidance and light visible. All banners are banners of loss; not even one banner of success is visible. The banner of Allah, through which the Arabs once overspread the world, is still present today. This banner still awaits a hand to raise it. There is need for some community or nation which will walk under this banner on the path of goodness, guidance, reform and salvation.

This is the account of profit and loss in this world. This worldly greatness is in itself a very great success, but if we compare it with the success of the Hereafter, it is very insignificant. The real profit and loss is that of the Hereafter. True profit and loss lie there, because it is a long life, a life that remains forever, and an everlasting abode. The real gain and the real loss are there: Paradise, the gain of Allah's pleasure, or Hell, the loss of Allah's displeasure. In the Hereafter, where a person may have reached his highest level of progress and perfection, or may have so squandered his humanity that he is lost in it, he will fall to the value of a stone, and in comfort and rest he will be lower than a stone.
﴿On the day when every person will see what he has sent forward, and the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾ (78:40). "On the day every person will see what he has earned and sent forward, and the disbeliever will say, 'Would that I were dust.'"

The truth is that this surah points out a decisive and plain path of truth; it shows that all paths are paths of loss, except
﴿Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and enjoined one another to truth and enjoined one another to patience﴾ (103:3). "Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and advise one another to truth, and advise one another to patience." And this is one path; there is no multiplicity in it. It is the path of faith and righteous deeds, the path of establishing an Islamic community, the path of a community which counsels the truth and enjoins goodness, whose ink is truth and whose wages are patience.

The truth is that the path is one. That is why, whenever two companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met each other, they would not part until they had recited Surah al-'Asr. After that, they would say salaam to each other and depart. In effect, they made a mutual covenant that they would follow this revolutionary constitution; they would bind themselves together that they would remain upon the path of righteous faith, continue to counsel the truth and enjoin patience, and pledge that they would remain the guardians of this constitution and members of the community that follows it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 104, verses 1–6 (part 1 of 3):

The question is: what is faith? …. We are not giving a jurisprudential explanation or definition of faith here. Our discussion is limited to the nature of faith, its value, and its effects on life.

Faith is in fact the connection that this small, limited, human creature establishes with the Reality that is eternal, everlasting and abiding, which is the origin of this universe and from which this universe came into existence. For this reason, this human being also becomes connected with the universe, in that both have one Creator. Then this human being becomes connected with the laws of nature according to which this world runs, and he becomes connected with the forces that operate in this universe. He comes out of the shell of his petty and limited self and enters into the vastness of the universe. In this way he steps beyond the bounds of his limited power and enters into the limitless forces that exist within this universe. The universe is so large in comparison to man that its boundaries are themselves beyond the reach of human knowledge. Then man steps out of the circle of his limited lifespan and enters the limitless times of existence and the times that come after the Resurrection.

The connection of human beings, which grants them this strength, this vastness and this freedom, also grants them the taste to enjoy this entire universe and its beauty, and to see the creatures that love his soul. Because of this connection, the brief journey of life becomes for man a journey of recreation, or a stroll through an exhibition that Allah has adorned for this human being in every place, every spot and every age. The truth is that this is a very great good fortune, a supreme joy and recreation, and a friendship with this whole universe. It is a wealth compared to which no other wealth has any value. It is also such a loss that if anyone is deprived of it, there is no greater loss or deficit than this.

Furthermore, the basic elements of faith are also the basic constituent elements of humanity:

(1) Through the worship of one God, a person is freed from all obedience, servitude and worship other than that of the One God. Thus the idea arises among people that all servants have one standing and are equal to one another. Therefore, it is not a reasonable attitude that a person should be granted the true blessing of freedom! This is the freedom that springs from the human conscience, and springs from the concept that exists as a real and factual truth, and that concept is that in this universe there is only one real power and one real object of worship. Accordingly, the natural demand of this conception of life and conception of the universe is that man be free, and the logical result of this belief is also that man be free.

(2) A person develops divinity (rabbaniyyah), and he derives all his concepts, all his values and standards, all his preferences, and his entire constitution and law from Allah. His relationships with Allah, with this universe, and with people are arranged in accordance with Allah's commands and laws. His personal desires and personal interests vanish from his life, and in their place Allah's Shariah and justice take over. In the consciousness of the believer, the value of his system of life becomes elevated, and his personality rises above the concepts and values of jahiliyyah (ignorance). Jahili preferences come to an end, and all the relationships that are based on earth, this world and material concepts come to an end, even if this person is an individual, because an individual believer too takes his concepts, values and preferences directly from Allah, since these values are indeed more exalted, more honourable, and more beneficial and worthy of consideration.

(3) As a result of faith, the relationship between Creator and creature is also determined.
